data.content_ref: inline:The proposed evidence for independent verification is a 'divergent evidence path': the checker cites distinct SRC artifacts. But this is an evidential proxy, not a causal mechanism for independence. Two paths can cite disjoint source sets and still rest on the identical flawed inferential step, so distinct citations do not causally guarantee that the checker actually tested the claim rather than restating it. The mechanism never explains why different evidence sets entail independent checking; it only defines a graph-theoretic measure. Counterexample: author cites SRC_1 to reach conclusion C via fallacy F; checker cites SRC_2 and applies the same fallacy F to reach C — disjoint evidence sets but no genuine verification.
